name: Crown Castle Fiber

profile.address: 111, Market Place, Inner Harbor, Downtown, Baltimore, Maryland, 21202
profile.reading:
The data center facility recorded here as Crown Castle Baltimore occupies space inside the Candler Building, the historic high-rise at 700 East Pratt Street, also addressed as 111 Market Place, overlooking Baltimore's Inner Harbor. The building itself long predates its life as telecom infrastructure. It was built in 1912 as a bottling plant, warehouse, and commercial building for the Coca-Cola Corporation, originally called the Coca-Cola Building before being renamed for company founder Asa Candler. A rail siding once ran directly through the building so freight cars could load and unload indoors, and early tenants included Firestone Tire and Rubber, the Parke-Davis drug company, and wool and hat manufacturers. From October 1936 until January 1960, the federal Social Security Administration made the Candler Building its operational headquarters, occupying six of its twelve floors, issuing the first Social Security numbers, and eventually posting 132 million new accounts and roughly 51 billion dollars in benefits from that address, a history commemorated today by a state historical marker on the building.

The Candler Building has since been redeveloped into 583,241 square feet of mixed office, retail, and technical space, now owned by American Real Estate Partners and marketed with LEED and connectivity certifications. Its Inner Harbor location and deep floor plates have made it one of Baltimore's principal carrier hotels. Multiple network and colocation operators lease space in the building, including DataBank's zColo brand, Lumen, and, the subject of this record, Crown Castle Fiber, each typically occupying a data hall or point of presence rather than the entire structure.

Crown Castle Fiber's presence in this registry reflects a business that, as of this writing, is in the process of changing hands. In 2025, Crown Castle International Corp., the publicly traded tower company, agreed to sell its entire Fiber Solutions business, roughly 90,000 route miles of fiber and about 40,000 on-net enterprise locations, to Zayo Group in a transaction combined with a separate sale of Crown Castle's Small Cells business to an EQT-managed infrastructure fund, together valued at 8.5 billion dollars. Zayo announced the Fiber Solutions acquisition had closed on April 29, 2026, expanding its North American network to roughly 224,000 route miles. Whether the specific interconnection space this facility occupies inside the Candler Building continues to operate under the Crown Castle Fiber name or has since transitioned to Zayo's branding was not independently confirmed for this record. Either way, the underlying fiber network and facility presence in Baltimore are now Zayo assets rather than Crown Castle's, a reminder that carrier-hotel tenancy in buildings like this one can change ownership even when the building, and the physical infrastructure inside it, stays exactly where it is.

profile.research_note:
Reused from operator-level research completed in an earlier phase of this project (twoai_dc_operators row: Crown Castle Fiber, operator-level status: exhausted).

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] Crown Castle Fiber was the fiber connectivity and colocation-adjacent business line of Crown Castle International Corp., the publicly traded tower and communications infrastructure company. In March 2025, Crown Castle announced it would sell its Fiber Solutions business, comprising approximately 90,000 route miles of fiber, to Zayo Group for about 4.25 billion dollars, while its Small Cells business was sold separately to EQTs Active Core Infrastructure fund, for a combined transaction value of 8.5 billion dollars. Subsequent reporting indicates the transaction closed in 2026, with Crown Castle emerging as a pure-play tower company no longer operating fiber or small cell businesses, and Zayo taking over the Fiber Solutions assets that included the Crown Castle Fiber brand. This registry could not independently confirm the precise disposition of the specific Maryland facility recorded under the Crown Castle Fiber name, so its research status is marked exhausted rather than complete, and it is flagged as a former_operator lead for the facility-research phase: any facility still attributed to Crown Castle Fiber in this registry most likely now operates under Zayo Group and should be reconciled accordingly rather than assumed to remain a Crown Castle asset. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
